diagnostics.message: `:resource.time_sleep.wait_for_aws_s3_bucket_settings` has an explicit `depends_on` on `:resource.aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block.origin`, but `:resource.aws_s3_bucket_policy.default` is already in the same `depends_on` list and itself declares `depends_on = [aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block.origin]`. Terraform dependencies are transitive, so the sleep already waits for the public access block; the direct entry (and the comment rationale) duplicates an existing edge and can be dropped.

`:resource.aws_cloudfront_distribution.default` lists `:resource.aws_s3_bucket.origin` in `depends_on`, but the distribution's origin already reads the bucket through `local.bucket_domain_name` -> `local.origin_bucket` -> `aws_s3_bucket.origin[0]` (`bucket_regional_domain_name` / `website_endpoint`), so the ordering is established implicitly by that attribute reference and the explicit `depends_on` entry is redundant (the bucket's readiness is additionally covered by the `aws_s3_bucket_ownership_controls.origin` / `time_sleep` entries, which are in turn created after the bucket).
